reallyusefulribbits.guide.name: Really Useful Ribbits
reallyusefulribbits.guide.subtitle: Jobs for swamp folk
reallyusefulribbits.guide.landing: This book is an addon guide. Ribbits already have professions in the original $(item)Ribbits$() mod. This addon teaches those same frogs to fish, farm, trade, and cause trouble.$(br2)If you lose the book, craft another from an ordinary $(item)book$() and a $(item)giant lily pad$().
reallyusefulribbits.guide.cat.intro.desc: What this addon changes, and what it leaves to the original Ribbits mod.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.cat.carry.desc: How to set a ribbit's home point with a maraca.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.cat.work.desc: How far ribbits look, how they share a village, and how to see their binds.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.cat.jobs.desc: What each original profession does once this addon is installed.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.welcome.1: Welcome. This guide is for players who already have $(item)Ribbits$() and want those frogs to do more than wander and play. The chapters go from setting a home with a maraca, to the work radius, to each profession.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.welcome.2: You do not have to read it all at once. Open a page when a fisher will not bite, a farmer stares at dirt, or a merchant will not stop croaking.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.welcome.3: A new copy can be made at a crafting table from an ordinary book and a giant lily pad from Ribbits.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.welcome.4: If you found a bug or just want to share feedback, you can leave it here: $(l:https://github.com/Nergan/really-useful-ribbits-mod/issues)https://github.com/Nergan/really-useful-ribbits-mod/issues$(/l)
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.addon.1: This addon does $(warn)not$() add new ribbit professions. Fishers, gardeners, merchants, sorcerers and nitwits already exist in $(item)Ribbits$(). They even have their own spawn eggs. What changes is what those frogs $(job)do$() after they spawn.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.addon.2: A ribbit is still one creature. The original mod picks its profession. This addon only watches that profession and gives it work: fishing, farming, trading, luck, or chaos.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.entry.head: Maracas
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.head.1: Right-click any ribbit with a $(item)maraca$() from the original $(item)Ribbits$() mod to set its home point where it is standing. Merchant ribbits sell maracas. You can no longer seat a ribbit on your head.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.head.2: Walk a worker closer to water, a farm or a chest, then click it with the maraca. Head-riding from this addon is gone.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.home.1: The home point is the same one from the original Ribbits mod. After a maraca click, the ribbit treats the block it stood on as home. That is how you relocate a worker without breaking the rest of its habits.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.home.2: Doing this also grants the advancement $(thing)so I guess this is my new home now…$(). The title follows the language of the client, like the rest of this book.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.radius.1: Working ribbits scan a radius for water, farms, containers, luck, endermen and sorcerer plant-growth. The default is $(thing)64$() blocks. Several ribbits may share the same ground. They will not steal a reserved crop tile or water block from each other.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.radius.2: Scan radius and sorcerer chaos are a $(thing)SERVER$() config: Mods → Really Useful Ribbits → Config, or the world file $(item)reallyusefulribbits-server.toml$(). Higher chaos flattens sorcerer odds. In multiplayer only the server value matters.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.highlight: Right-click a fisher or a farmer to glow the ribbit and sprinkle particles on its container and water tile or farm. You will hear a beacon chime. No extra blocks or shulkers appear.
If that ribbit has no water, farm or container yet, it croaks in pain and angry particles appear instead. Give it time to look around, or move it closer to what it needs.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.fisherman: A fisher binds one nearby water block and one container (chest, barrel, shulker, double chest, and the like). It sits on the bank with its fishing pose and fishes like a player: splashes gather at the bobber, then it reels in. The catch goes into a single slot that holds 16 items.

A catch shows happy villager stars, the fishing bobber splash, and a quiet orb ping. The fisher sits on the water's edge. Fish dropped nearby with $(thing)Q$() are picked up. When the bag is full it carries the catch to its container and returns.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.farmer.1: A gardener binds one connected farm and one container. A farm is a cluster of farmland (including Farmer's Delight farmland), soul sand, or sugar-cane bases that touch each other inside the scan radius. Inventory is four slots of 64.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.farmer.2: It works like a little straw golem: harvest ripe crops first (pumpkins and melons as the fruit blocks, not the stems), then replant, then walk the produce to its chest. It walks up to the chest; it will not insert or take items from across the field. One gardener covers ordinary farmland, soul sand, checkerboard cane and glow-berry vines in the same radius. Watering is short and infrequent: it wets farmland and sometimes coaxes glow berries onto vines. It only tills a dirt hole boxed in on all four sides.
A merchant has 27 slots of 256. It starts with a few random goods plus 256 emeralds and 256 amethyst shards. It visits other traders and copies the items they sell, then builds up to twice as many amethyst sell offers as a typical stall — an average of the shops it has seen.
Happy villager stars appear when the stall refreshes. Glow particles follow it while it chases a player. Right-click opens its offers. Each item type appears only once. It always walks at 1.5× speed.
Right-click a sorcerer with an $(item)amethyst shard$() — the shard is spent — and it looks at you, then rolls a spell that can actually happen. Growth, weather, a diamond rain, a safe dimension hop, lightning that does not hurt the frog, a fire ring, an invisible trip to a real structure, rare flight, 1–16 summoned mobs, or 1–8 tamed pets in random colors (modded pets included when they can be tamed).

Rarer rolls: a giant glowing phantom ($(thing)Foma, is that you?$()), an hour as a spectator ($(thing)This ghost will be kind, right?$()), a blast ten times larger that the frog itself ignores ($(thing)no magic today$()), or a rare morph ($(thing)hexed :($()) — only humanoid mobs can still place, break and open things. Anyone else can only feed the sorcerer an $(item)enchanted golden apple$(). That apple also follows the frog the same way an amethyst shard does, and strips every curse for $(thing)Get this off me!$(). Clicking empty-handed makes the frog angry. Chaos starts a bit higher. Endermen flee. Very rarely — a dragon and $(thing)You asked for it$().
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.nitwit.1: A nitwit still applies $(thing)Luck$() inside the scan radius. It also picks up loot on the ground: it walks to the item and takes it. The bag is 27 slots of 64.
reallyusefulribbits.guide.page.nitwit.2: Once it is carrying something, it sometimes walks up to a player and tosses the items the way a player drops them with $(thing)Q$(). It will not fish, farm, or trade. A maraca still sets its home.
